writeup: TIC 79792004 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 15.2462 days. Automated analysis of TESS photometry detected a primary eclipse causing a 0.09% dimming of the star's light, with a signal-to-noise ratio of 12.6. A secondary eclipse was not detected. Pixel-level image analysis using difference imaging confirmed the signal at the target location with a peak signal-to-noise of 8.0, though the centroid offset measured 13.2 arcsec from the target star. The object does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel candidate. The pipeline's machine-learning classifier assigned it a score of 0.77, indicating moderately high confidence that this represents a real eclipsing system rather than instrumental noise or stellar variability.
